content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, a garment most commonly symbolizes a person's spiritual state or standing before God — above all, righteousness. Being clothed in clean, white, or fine garments represents righteousness (whether imputed righteousness received from God/Christ or the righteous deeds of the saints), salvation, and acceptance before God; conversely, soiled, filthy, or inadequate garments represent sin, guilt, and unrighteousness. The dominant reading is 'the garment of salvation / robe of righteousness' — the believer is stripped of sin-stained clothing and clothed by God with righteousness, often expressed as being 'clothed with Christ.'", "primary_basis": ["Isaiah 61:10 ('he has clothed me with garments of salvation; he has covered me with the robe of righteousness')", "Zechariah 3:3-5 (Joshua the high priest's filthy garments removed and replaced with clean/rich robes, explicitly interpreted as removal of iniquity)", "Isaiah 64:6 ('all our righteous deeds are like filthy rags/a polluted garment')", "Revelation 19:8 (fine linen, bright and pure, 'for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints')", "Revelation 3:4-5, 3:18; 7:13-14 (white garments; robes washed and made white in the blood of the Lamb)", "Matthew 22:11-12 (parable of the wedding feast: the man without a wedding garment cast out — widely read as lacking the righteousness required for entry)", "Galatians 3:27 ('as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ'); Romans 13:14", "Genesis 3:21 (God clothing Adam and Eve with skins, frequently read as God's provision of covering for sin)", "Ephesians 4:22-24; Colossians 3:9-14 (putting off the old self and putting on the new)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Covering for sin/shame and atonement: the garment as God's provision to cover human nakedness, guilt, and shame, prefiguring atonement (often tied to sacrifice in the Genesis 3:21 skins). Closely related to, and often merged with, the righteousness reading.", "basis": ["Genesis 3:7, 3:21", "Isaiah 61:10", "Revelation 3:18 ('white garments so that... the shame of your nakedness may not be seen')"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Identity, status, office, or authority: garments mark who a person is — royal robes, priestly vestments, the prophetic mantle passed from Elijah to Elisha, Joseph's coat. Tearing garments signals grief or loss of status; giving a robe confers honor or succession.", "basis": ["Exodus 28 (priestly garments 'for glory and for beauty')", "1 Kings 19:19; 2 Kings 2:13-14 (Elijah's mantle)", "Genesis 37:3 (Joseph's robe)", "1 Samuel 18:4 (Jonathan giving David his robe)", "Esther 6:8-9; Luke 15:22 (the best robe for the returning son)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The old and new self / moral character and conduct: 'putting off' vices and 'putting on' virtues as a change of moral clothing; character as what one wears.", "basis": ["Ephesians 4:22-24", "Colossians 3:8-14", "1 Peter 5:5 ('clothe yourselves with humility')", "Job 29:14 ('I put on righteousness, and it clothed me')"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The body, resurrection, and immortality: the mortal body as a garment/tent to be exchanged for a glorified, immortal covering; used in discussions of resurrection and the intermediate state.", "basis": ["2 Corinthians 5:1-4 ('longing to put on our heavenly dwelling... that we may not be found naked')", "1 Corinthians 15:53-54 ('this perishable must put on the imperishable')"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Readiness, watchfulness, and preparedness for the Lord's return: keeping one's garments so as not to be found naked or unprepared; girding the loins for service.", "basis": ["Revelation 16:15 ('Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps his garments on')", "Luke 12:35 ('Stay dressed for action')", "Exodus 12:11"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Baptismal symbolism in liturgical/patristic tradition: the white baptismal garment as the putting on of Christ and the restoration of the robe of glory lost at the Fall (prominent in Eastern/Syriac fathers, e.g., Ephrem's 'robe of glory').", "basis": ["Galatians 3:27", "Genesis 3:21 read alongside baptismal practice", "patristic and liturgical usage rather than a single proof text"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "Garment imagery is pervasive and multivalent in Scripture, but there is a recognizable center of gravity in Christian interpretation: garments symbolize one's spiritual condition and standing before God, with clean/white garments as righteousness and salvation and filthy garments as sin. A well-known intra-consensus debate concerns Revelation 19:8 and the wedding garment of Matthew 22 — whether the garment is imputed righteousness (a common Protestant emphasis) or the righteous deeds/sanctified life of believers; both remain within the same broad symbolic field. The alternative readings listed (status/office, old-new self, resurrection body, watchfulness, baptism) are materially distinct uses that context determines, and standard reference works treat all of them, with righteousness/salvation as the leading entry."}
